newsitem.title: USA: Donald Maude dies at 55, was Scotia economist.
newsitem.headline: Donald Maude dies at 55, was Scotia economist.

text.p: Donald E. Maude, chief U.S. economist and fixed-income strategist at Scotia Capital Markets (USA) Inc., died last Thursday at Beekman Hospital after suffering a heart attack, a spokeswoman for the firm said.

Highly regarded in the Wall Street community, Maude had been at Scotia for five years. Previously he was chief financial economist and chairman of the interest rate policy committee and managing director for Merrill Lynch Capital Markets from 1978 to 1984.
"Don was a man of great personal warmth and humor and a mentor to many," said Ted Price, chairman and chief executive of Scotia.
Maude's death came as "quite a surprise," said a worker at Scotia.

He was a member of the board of directors of Scotia McCloud in the U.S. and Canada. Maude was a member of the Monetary Policy Forum, Money Marketeers of New York, the Downtown Business Economics Club of New York and National Association of Business Economists. He was a former trustee of Monmouth University in West Long Branch, N.J.
Maude earned his bachelor's degree from Monmouth, a master's degree from the University of Missouri and had done doctoral work at Princeton University.
He is survived by his wife, Kathleen; a son, Kevin, and a daughter Alison. The John E. Day Funeral Home in Red Bank, N.J., was in charge of arrangements.
(( John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1663 ))
